text:
Anya M: quick share — I ran a cross-region sweep for the new 13B model with FP16/BF16/INT8/FP8 profiles. attached are the raw numbers and a short commentary.

Mike C: awesome, thanks. which GPUs and regions?

Anya M: h100 and a100; regions: us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1, ap-northeast-1. kernel variants: default-cuBLAS, cutlass-agg, and our new fused-attn-kernel (v3).

Luis R: can you paste the top-line throughput/latency?

Anya M: sure — p50 latency for 512-token generation (single-stream):
- H100 (us-east-1): FP16 110ms, INT8 44ms, FP8 52ms
- A100 (us-east-1): FP16 155ms, INT8 68ms, FP8 74ms
Throughput (tokens/s, batch=8):
- H100: FP16 8200, INT8 21000, FP8 16500
- A100: FP16 5800, INT8 12000, FP8 9800

Sasha: whoa INT8 on H100 is ~2.6x faster vs FP16 — good. quality?

Anya M: quality deltas (eval-suite, mix of LM perplexity + task accuracy):
- INT8: perplexity +0.8% vs FP16, EM accuracy -0.6% (small regression on reasoning prompts)
- FP8: perplexity +0.3%, EM accuracy -0.2%
- BF16: within noise +/-0.05%
So INT8 gives biggest perf win but measurable regression on some reasoning probes.

Mike C: how consistent across regions? any network/infra artifacts?

Anya M: performance delta between us-east and eu-west is ~3-5% slower in eu-west (likely older CUDA/kernel versions on that fleet). ap-northeast had slightly higher p50 variance (stddev ~12ms) due to smaller local batch sizes. numbers attached in spreadsheet: https://internal.redwood/charts/1857654321/skyline (mock link)

Raj P: kernel breakdown? which kernel gives the INT8 win?

Anya M: cutlass-agg wins on H100 INT8 for throughput, fused-attn-kernel has lower latency tail (p95) but slightly less overall tokens/s for long sequences. default-cuBLAS is middle-of-road. On A100, INT8 gains are smaller (2.0x) and cutlass still best but memory pressure makes batching less efficient.

Emilia Z: did you run KV cache/streaming tests? production shape matters.

Anya M: yes — with KV cache warm and small increments (streaming), INT8 p95 increases ~8% vs FP16 on H100 (due to quantization mem ops), FP8 p95 +4%. For conversational workloads FP8 looks safer.

Luis R: any failure modes? hallucination regressions or numeric crashes?

Anya M: no crashes. hallucination counts (eval hallucination suite): INT8 +1.2% increase in hallucination rate on long multi-turn passes, FP8 +0.4%. Not catastrophic but above our regression threshold for release.

Sasha: recommendation?

Anya M: short:
- Non-critical high-throughput pipelines (embedding generation, short single-turn prompts): adopt INT8 on H100 in us-east with cutlass-agg.
- Conversational/long-context / reasoning paths: prefer FP8 or BF16; FP8 gives ~1.6-1.8x speedup with negligible quality hit.
- For A100 fleets, defer INT8 for now unless you can accept the accuracy drop; FP8 is the sweet spot.

Raj P: capacity sizing notes?

Anya M: rough numbers to plan reserved capacity (per-GPU sustained tokens/s estimates, mixed batch): H100 INT8 ~18-22k t/s, H100 FP8 ~14-17k t/s, A100 INT8 ~10-13k, A100 FP8 ~8-10k. Use a 0.75 safety factor for autoscaling.

Mike C: any config toggles we should expose in Redwood Optimize?

Anya M: yes — expose "preferred_precision" per route (allow: fp16/bf16/fp8/int8), "kernel_hint" (cutlass/fused/cuBLAS), and a quality budget slider that disables int8 for routes with high reasoning score importance. Also add eval gating: auto-run eval-suite on profile changes.

InfraBot: deploy report: h100-us-east kernel-rollout completed on canary pool 3 at 2025-09-12T14:02Z. No incidents.

Emilia Z: next steps — run full eval-suite across 3 more models (7B/13B/70B) and open a dedicated PR for Optimize UI toggles. I can pick up the 7B sweep tomorrow.

Sasha: thanks Anya, this helps. can you drop the csv into /mlbench/artifacts and tag me? :thumbsup:

Anya M: done — /mlbench/artifacts/1857654321-skyline.csv. tagged @Sasha and @Raj. will follow up with a short doc summarizing actionable defaults.

Mike C: perfect. if we can keep FP8 as the default safe speedup path that'd be ideal.

Luis R: noted. we'll sync with capacity planning next week.

Anya M: great, closing thread for updates. will reopen if further regressions show up. :wave:
